title: Tara's Red Bean Plant
summary: For her birthday, Tara gets red bean seeds and a gardening book. She plants and waters with great excitement, but the plant starts to wilt. What went wrong?
pages:
On her birthday, Mom gave Tara a special present.
"Wow! Red beans and a book about gardening," said Tara. "Now I can grow my very own bean plant."

First, plant the seed, Tara read.
So she planted it.
"You're doing great, Tara!" the book told her.
Now water it. La la la! Tara sang, and did just that.

"Soon my plant will be big," Tara told her friends.
"You have to water it a lot so it will be healthy," they said. "Just like children need to drink lots of milk to grow up big and strong!"

A few days later, the bean sprouted.
"Look, Mom!" Tara called. "It's growing!"

The next morning, Tara watered the plant again.
"La la la! Drink, drink, drink!" she sang. "If you drink more water, you'll grow faster!"
"Oh dear, Tara, not like that!" said the book.

At noon Tara watered it again. La la la!
"Oh dear, Tara!" said the book, louder now. "My pages say you don't water a plant at noon."

But Tara kept on watering. La la la, la la la!
"Oh dear, Tara! You forgot to read me!"

The next day, as she left for school, Tara asked Mom:
"Please give my plant some more water at noon!"
"Did you read the book?" asked Mom.
"My pages say you water the plant only once a day," the book said sadly. Oh dear, Tara!
Three days later, Tara was sad too. "My poor plant!" she cried.

At school she talked with her friends. "I take such good care of my plant. Why is it so sad?"
"What does the book say?" they asked.
"Oh dear," said Tara. "I stopped reading it."

At home, Tara showed Mom the plant. "Sorry, Mom," said Tara. "Now I'm going to read the book."
"That's a wonderful idea," Mom answered.
Don't water the plant too much, or the roots get soggy, Tara read. Then the leaves wilt and turn brown.
"I'm so sorry, Red Bean," Tara whispered.
"The plant won't be sad, because it knows you love it," said Mom. "You can show it your love by learning how to take care of it the right way."
"And you can say sorry to the book, too, because you ignored it. It needs you to pay attention to it as well!"
A few days later, the red bean plant was healthy again. And now Tara and her gardening book were best friends!
